newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Tel Aviv stock trading system to begin August 14.
newsitem.headline: Tel Aviv stock trading system to begin August 14.

text.p: The board of Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE) approved plans on Thursday to begin continuous computerised trading on August 14, even if all the exchange's members are not fully linked up, a spokeswoman said.
Etti Tutnauer told Reuters that all the exchange's members are connected to the trading system but it is possibile some members would only be linked as far as their dealing rooms.
The system is designed to enable members to relay trading information in real time to their branches around the country but Tutnauer said some members may not be ready do that by August 14.

The TASE now uses a system it calls "semi-continuous trading" for its heavy capitalisation shares. The new system is aimed at making the Israeli market more closely resemble trading systems elsewhere around the world.

Continuous trading will begin with the top 10 shares that are now traded in the Mishtanim framework but not part of the Maof blue chip index. Tutnauer said the final list would be determined before trading begins.
